title: G3 (MAIN): Merging/orthogonalization — optimal POVM can be made projective

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Claim (crux).** Any optimal rank-one POVM for a two-state ensemble can be transformed without decreasing $I(X;Y)$ into a von Neumann (projective) measurement; i.e. the optimal directions can be taken mutually orthogonal.

**Binary-convexity route.** Write $I(X;Y)=H(p_1,p_2)-\sum_y a_y\,h\!\big(\tfrac{(a_y+b_y)/2}{a_y}\big)$ with $h$ binary entropy. The posterior of outcome $y$ depends on $|\phi_y\rangle$ only via $b_y/a_y=\langle\phi_y|\Delta|\phi_y\rangle/\langle\phi_y|\sigma|\phi_y\rangle$. Take two outcomes spanning a common 2D subspace $V$; among all POVMs on $V$ with the same $E+E'=:\Pi|_V$, show replacing them by the orthogonal pair (eigenvectors of $\Delta|_V$ relative to $\sigma|_V$) does not decrease $I$, by convexity. Iterate.

**Sub-claims to prove in full:**
(i) *Feasibility:* orthogonal replacement preserves $\sum_y E_y=I$ globally — must be done in a 2D invariant block.
(ii) *No loss:* identify the exact convex function and verify inequality direction + equality cases.
(iii) *Termination & completeness:* iteration ends in a complete orthogonal family summing to $I$, with no non-orthogonal leftovers.

**$N=2$ is essential.** False for $N\ge3$ (Holevo/Peres trine states need a non-projective 3-outcome POVM). Any argument that also applies to $N=3$ is wrong; the proof must use the single ratio $b_y/a_y$ governing the binary posterior. Refs: Levitin (1995); Holevo, *Probabilistic and Statistical Aspects of Quantum Theory*.
